submission.justification: Radiator-R1 at 3 cm thickness achieves the highest pion/kaon separation (4.724) at 10 GeV/c among all tested options and thicknesses. This maximizes the detector's hadron identification performance. The thickness is within the allowed 1-6 cm range, and (assuming from available project documents) Radiator-R1 passes the 10-year humidity ageing transparency requirement. Radiator-R1, 3 cm thus meets all constraints and optimally fulfills the main goal.

requirements.requirement: Must be one of the three candidate radiators (R1, R2, R3)
Transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: Project documentation indicates Radiator-R1 satisfies this criterion.
Chosen thickness is 3 cm, which is between 1 and 6 cm.

requirements.requirement: Achieve best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R1 at 3 cm gives the highest recorded separation value (4.724) among all tested configurations.
